lede.headline: Dell's record AI backlog headlines blowout quarter
lede.dek: Dell posted record fiscal third-quarter results, including a $132.3 billion AI server backlog, as revenue more than doubled to $54.9 billion. The company raised its full-year guidance across every metric and added $25 billion to its buyback authorization.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Dell's record AI backlog headlines blowout quarter
stories.move: Dell reported fiscal third-quarter (ended Oct. 30) revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% year over year, with AI-optimized server revenue of $22.0 billion, up 291%. Operating income rose 251% to $7.4 billion and diluted EPS rose 287% to $8.82. The company booked $60.2 billion of AI orders in the quarter, ending with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog, returned $4.9 billion to shareholders, and added $25.0 billion to its buyback authorization. Dell raised full-year revenue guidance to $202.0 billion from $192.0 billion and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $29.68 from $25.50.
stories.why: The results show AI server demand still accelerating industry-wide, even as some rivals have flagged supply constraints this earnings season.
stories.bear: Dell's own Q4 guidance implies revenue growth slowing to about 69% from Q3's 103%, and a backlog this concentrated in AI hardware orders can swing sharply if even one large customer delays.
stories.watch: Dell's fiscal Q4 guidance of $56.3 billion revenue; the fiscal year ends Jan. 29, 2027.

stories.headline: Alibaba's AI Cloud growth accelerates to 53%
stories.move: Alibaba reported revenue of 271.5 billion yuan (about $38B) for the September quarter, up 10% year over year and above analyst estimates. AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue rose 53% to 61.0 billion yuan, faster than the prior quarter's 45% growth. Non-GAAP net income was 19.9 billion yuan, up 92% from 10.4 billion yuan a year earlier.
stories.why: The acceleration in AI Cloud growth suggests Chinese cloud demand is still ramping even as Alibaba and its rivals pour money into AI infrastructure.
stories.bear: Free cash flow turned negative as the AI buildout consumes cash, and some outlets reported adjusted per-share earnings missed consensus despite the headline beat.
stories.watch: Whether AI Cloud's growth rate keeps accelerating next quarter as new chip export rules take effect.

stories.headline: NetEase revenue slips as it raises its dividend
stories.move: NetEase reported third-quarter net revenue of 27.9 billion yuan ($4.2 billion), down 1.8% year over year. Games and related services revenue fell 1.7% to 22.9 billion yuan, and Youdao revenue dropped 12.3%. Net income attributable to shareholders was 8.4 billion yuan, down from 8.62 billion a year earlier. The board raised its quarterly dividend to $0.117 per ordinary share ($0.585 per ADS), payable to holders of record as of Dec. 3.
stories.why: The results show one of China's largest gaming companies still raising its payout to shareholders even as its core games business contracts.
stories.bear: A second straight quarter of declining games revenue raises questions about whether new titles can offset the slowdown before Ananta's January 2027 global launch.
stories.watch: Ananta's multiplatform global launch, currently scheduled for Jan. 15, 2027.

stories.headline: PDD's profit grows even as revenue growth stalls
stories.move: PDD Holdings, the owner of Temu and Pinduoduo, reported third-quarter revenue of 108.3 billion yuan, roughly flat year over year. Transaction-services revenue fell 12% to 48.5 billion yuan, while online marketing revenue rose 12% to 59.8 billion yuan. Operating profit rose 25% to 31.2 billion yuan, with operating margin up 5.7 percentage points to 28.8%. Net income attributable to ordinary shareholders was 29.5 billion yuan, up slightly from 29.3 billion a year earlier, and the company held 455 billion yuan in cash and short-term investments, up 8% from year-end.
stories.why: Operating profit grew even as overall revenue stalled, suggesting PDD is cutting costs and subsidies rather than competing purely on price.
stories.bear: Flat overall revenue, after years of rapid growth, and a 12% drop in transaction-services revenue point to intensifying competition in Chinese e-commerce.
stories.watch: Whether Temu's US tariff-related cost pressure shows up more clearly in fourth-quarter margins.

stories.headline: SpaceX stock drifts back near its June IPO price
stories.move: SpaceX shares closed at $133.35 on Monday, close to the company's $135 June IPO price, after falling as low as $127.79 on Nov. 20 - briefly dipping below the offer price. The stock had traded near $145 the prior week before a rally tied to Anthropic's Nov. 19 IPO faded into a broadly weak session, according to The Motley Fool. Anthropic's IPO filing disclosed a commitment to spend up to $120.5 billion through 2029 on computing capacity from SpaceX's AI computing arm.
stories.why: A major AI customer committing over $100 billion to SpaceX's computing business is now sitting alongside a stock price near its offer level, a sign investor enthusiasm for the AI buildout has cooled since the June debut.
stories.bear: A stock trading near its IPO price five months after a record debut raises questions about whether the offering was priced too aggressively, or whether sentiment toward AI infrastructure spending has genuinely shifted.
stories.watch: SpaceX's 180-day post-IPO lockup, which the company's own disclosures put at Dec. 8, freeing insider shares for sale.

stories.headline: Arista's Bechtolsheim sells $56M more stock
stories.move: Arista Networks co-founder Andreas von Bechtolsheim sold about 300,000 shares on Nov. 18, in 13 lots at prices between $183.60 and $195.17, for a total of about $56.1 million. The Form 4 was filed Nov. 20 and left him with 179,455,156 shares.
stories.why: The sale continues a pattern of steady, incremental selling rather than a reaction to any single event at Arista.
stories.bear: Repeated large sales by a co-founder, even on a scheduled basis, steadily reduce his ownership stake over time.
stories.watch: Arista's next earnings report, expected in February 2027.

stories.headline: Tether leaders' fund holds 27.9% of a gold royalty firm
stories.move: A Nov. 23 SEC filing shows Tether Global Investments Fund, S.I.C.A.F., S.A. - whose reporting persons include Tether chairman Giancarlo Devasini, CEO Paolo Ardoino and director Jean-Louis van der Velde - beneficially owns 21,354,627 shares, or 27.9%, of Elemental Royalty Corp, a gold and silver streaming and royalty company listed on Nasdaq and the TSX Venture Exchange. The amendment discloses an internal transfer of 7,502,502 shares between two Tether-affiliated entities on Sept. 2, 2026; it does not report a change in the fund's own stake.
stories.why: It shows Tether's leadership continuing to hold a large stake in hard assets like gold and silver royalties, alongside the company's bitcoin holdings.
stories.bear: The filing reports only an internal transfer between Tether-affiliated entities, not new buying, so it may say little about the group's current investment appetite.
stories.watch: Any further Schedule 13D amendments disclosing a change in the fund's Elemental Royalty stake.

watch: Dec. 1: Jensen Huang's closed-door testimony before three House committees on Nvidia's China ties.
Dec. 1: Adobe's Shantanu Narayen hands the CEO role to Anil Chakravarthy and becomes executive chair.
Dec. 3: The Senate Banking Committee's requested hearing date for Jensen Huang, with a subpoena possible if he declines.
Dec. 3: NetEase's raised dividend record date.
Dec. 8: SpaceX's 180-day post-IPO lockup expires, freeing insider shares for sale.
quickHits: Nvidia shares fell 7.2% Tuesday to $153.17, giving back part of Monday's Jensen Huang reinstatement rally, per Finnhub pricing data.
Blackstone-affiliated funds bought about 388,000 shares of Blackstone Private Real Estate Credit & Income Fund for roughly $10.2 million on Nov. 20, a Nov. 23 Form 4 showed.
memo: A leadership reversal can move a stock 30% in a day, but it's the underlying order book - like Dell's record AI backlog - that sustains the move.
Several of the world's biggest tech companies (Alibaba, NetEase, PDD) are all seeing margins squeezed by AI capex at once - a sector-wide pattern, not a company-specific problem.
Recurring, pre-scheduled insider stock sales are usually set up months in advance - don't read short-term signals into a long-running selling program.
